title: Finite partial monitoring: signal feedback and observability classes
summary: After acting, the learner receives only the feedback specified by a public signal matrix; the true loss may remain hidden. The objective is to compete with the best fixed action. Local and global observability must be determined jointly from the loss and signal matrices.

description_paragraphs: After acting, the learner receives only the feedback specified by a public signal matrix; the true loss may remain hidden. The objective is to compete with the best fixed action. Local and global observability must be determined jointly from the loss and signal matrices.

model.instance: The finite game $G=(L,H)$ is fixed and public, with $L\in[0,1]^{K\times M}$ and signal map H on action/outcome pairs. The environment fixes hidden outcomes $o_{1:T}\in[M]^T$ in advance. Only the signal is observed after acting. Duplicate and degenerate actions are excluded. Local and global observability are region-specific cases.

assumptions.scope: The objects, time horizon, and variable blocks explicitly declared here; none is inherited from another specification.
assumptions.description: For every action $a$ and outcome $o$, $0\le L(a,o)\le1$.

assumptions.scope: The objects, time horizon, and variable blocks explicitly declared here; none is inherited from another specification.
assumptions.description: Let $C_i=\{p\in\Delta_M:\ell_i^\top p\le\ell_j^\top p\text{ for all }j\}$. Duplicate actions with identical loss rows are excluded, as are degenerate actions whose nonempty cell $C_i$ is strictly contained in another cell $C_j$. Dominated actions with empty cells are permitted.

assumptions.scope: The objects, time horizon, and variable blocks explicitly declared here; none is inherited from another specification.
assumptions.description: The complete signal matrix H is public, but each round reveals only H(a_t,o_t), generally insufficient to recover o_t or the incurred loss L(a_t,o_t).

model.parameter_domain_description: G: a finite matrix/map pair (public); K: $K\in\mathbb N,\ K\ge2$ (public); M: $M\in\mathbb N,\ M\ge2$ (public); T: $T\in\mathbb N,\ T\ge1$ (public); v: $v\ge0$, finite on the relevant observability branch (public).
interaction_timing: Full tables $L,H$ are public; the outcome sequence $o_{1:T}$ is fixed and hidden.
After revealing only $H(a_t,o_t)$, proceed to the next round.
model.adversary_information: The environment fixes the entire loss sequence before interaction. It may know the algorithm and public parameters but cannot depend on the learner’s private seed. This is an oblivious-adversary specification and does not automatically extend to history-dependent adaptive adversaries.
unresolved_applicability: A fixed-game classification by the exponent of T does not certify joint optimality in game size or observability-estimator constants. Degenerate games are handled separately.

observability_definitions.signal_matrix: Each row of S_a corresponds to a distinct symbol of H(a,·), with (S_a)_{s,o}=1{H(a,o)=s}.
observability_definitions.global: Every difference of loss rows $\ell_i-\ell_j$ lies in the sum of the images of all $S_a^{\mathsf T}$.
observability_definitions.local: For adjacent Pareto-optimal cells i and j sharing a face of dimension M-2, the row difference can be reconstructed from the image spaces of S_a^T for actions in that neighborhood.
observability_definitions.scope: Local and global conditions are used in different comparison regions. The fixed nondegenerate-game specification does not impose them simultaneously.

description_paragraphs: Entries of the public loss matrix $L$ lie in $[0,1]$. Knowing the matrix does not reveal the current hidden outcome column $o_t$.
The public signal map $H$ takes arbitrary finite symbols; signals need not equal numerical losses.
The hidden outcome sequence $o_{1:T}$ is oblivious and fixed before interaction.

The public finite game is $G=(L,H)$. Let $C_i$ be the outcome-distribution region where action $i$ is optimal. Duplicate loss rows and degenerate actions with nonempty $C_i$ strictly contained in another $C_j$ are excluded. Local/global observability defines comparison branches rather than simultaneous model assumptions.
Fix the game $G$ satisfying $K,M\ge2$. Actions lie in $[K]$, outcomes in $[M]$, and signals in the finite range of the matrix $H$.
The game classification holds with only $T$ growing. It does not establish joint minimax optimality in $K,M$ and estimator constant $v$.

operations.query_signature: Inputs: $t,\ a_t\in[K]$. Timing and visible information follow the specified protocol.
operations.order_convention: order is relative to the current member f_t(x), f(x), or sample F(x;ξ_t) of the named indexed function family and only with respect to x; finite feedback interfaces have no derivative order

feedback_quality.description: The outcome $o_t$ is fixed but hidden. The learner first selects $a_t$, incurs $L(a_t,o_t)$, and observes only $H(a_t,o_t)$. Neither the outcome nor the incurred loss is revealed unless recoverable from the signal and public tables. No signal from a second action in the same round is available.

operations.coupling: The outcome $o_t$ is fixed but hidden. The learner first selects $a_t$, incurs $L(a_t,o_t)$, and observes only $H(a_t,o_t)$. Neither the outcome nor the incurred loss is revealed unless recoverable from the signal and public tables. No signal from a second action in the same round is available.
operations.index_control: The learner selects feasible actions and explicitly permitted probes. The environment controls the current loss, outcome, or fresh sample; the learner cannot select future rounds.
operations.access_schedule: Follow the interaction order in registry.protocols exactly. Current loss feedback follows the action; any pre-action context or advice phase is specified separately.

auxiliary_interfaces: No additional access to hidden losses, means, or gradients is available. Projection, sampling, and internal optimization over public domains may have separately recorded computation costs; they are not free loss oracles.
description_paragraphs: Action-outcome signal:

$$
t,\ a_t\in[K]\ \longmapsto\ Y_t=H(a_t,o_t)
$$
The environment outcome $o_t$ is already fixed but hidden when the learner chooses action $a_t$.
The learner incurs $L(a_t,o_t)$ and observes only the signal $H(a_t,o_t)$.
The outcome $o_t$ and incurred loss are hidden unless inferable from the signal and public matrices.
No signal from a second action in the same round is supplied.
Public inputs: $T$ and the complete fixed game $G=(L,H)$.

output.feasibility: Every loss-bearing action must belong to the action domain. The final output retains the complete action trajectory.
output.allowed_postprocessing: Any measurable computation on received feedback is allowed. No native observation may be added after the budget is exhausted or the algorithm stops.
output.certificate_requirement: Only the stated statistical guarantee is required, not a certificate verifiable through the feedback interface.
description_paragraphs: The output is the complete action trajectory satisfying feasibility and timing requirements. Randomized mixtures may be implemented before acting. Retrospective averages or convex combinations cannot replace actions that have already incurred loss. No additional optimal value or certificate is required.

metric.normalization: Use the cumulative quantity over T rounds without dividing by T. Preserve the displayed order of probability or expectation.
metric.finiteness_conditions: The entries of L lie in [0,1], so cumulative excess loss lies in [−T,T]. The fixed-game classification tracks only T.
description_paragraphs:
$$
R_T=\sum_tL(a_t,o_t)-\min_{a\in[K]}\sum_tL(a,o_t),\qquad Y_t=H(a_t,o_t)
$$

components.description: Sequential online rounds; only information permitted by the protocol is visible in each round.
One signal is observed per round, for T signal events. No fictitious gradient or function-value charges are introduced.

resource.budget_semantics: There are T sequential interaction rounds. Native feedback count is determined by the per-round protocol and is not an independent budget to minimize.
resource.scalarization: At fixed T, compare the native cumulative quantity in the objective. Retain the full resource vector; internal optimization, projection, and sampling are not implicitly one loss query.
resource.setup_cost: Only declared public inputs may be read. Hidden losses, means, or samples cannot be accessed in advance or outside the $T$ rounds or $\tau$ samples.
resource.online_cost: All causal randomized strategies are allowed. Public-game preprocessing, cell and observability calculations, and internal policy optimization are charged separately; an information-theoretic existence upper bound does not automatically supply an efficient implementation.
resource.amortization_scope: The algorithm runs on one environment. Charged feedback cannot be reused across independent instances.
resource.precision_model: Observations and internal arithmetic use the exact-real model. No bit-complexity claim follows.

Information calls, arithmetic, communication rounds, and memory are measured separately. Exact real internal computation is excluded from information complexity unless explicitly charged. This does not imply a bit-complexity bound.

algorithms.randomization: Private randomization is allowed. The seed is hidden from the environment and independent of the fixed instance and sample randomness.
algorithms.adaptivity: The action and every probe in a round may depend only on previous-round feedback, public inputs, any context or advice already revealed that round, and private randomness. They may not use unrevealed current losses or samples.
restrictions: All measurable causal policies satisfying the declared information timing and feasible domain are allowed, without extra span, iteration-form, or polynomial-time restrictions.
algorithms.internal_computation: Arbitrary measurable exact-real computation and all causal randomized policies are permitted. Feedback complexity does not imply arithmetic or bit complexity. Public-game preprocessing, cell and observability calculations, and internal policy optimization are separate costs. An information-theoretic existence bound does not certify an efficient implementation.
algorithms.parallelism: Online rounds proceed sequentially. A two-point evaluation is a same-round feedback pair, not two independent rounds.
description_paragraphs: All measurable causal randomized policies respecting the stated timing are allowed. The private seed is independent of the fixed instance and future samples. Apart from explicit feedback, output, and budget requirements, there are no restrictions on linear spans, iteration form, internal arithmetic, memory, or communication.

guarantees.complete_expression: The native objective is $R_T^*(G)=\inf_{\mathcal A\,\mathrm{knowing}\,G}\sup_{o_{1:T}\in[M]^T}\mathbb E_{\mathcal A}[R_T]$.
aggregation_order: The game G=(L,H) is fixed and public. It is not part of the worst-case variables in this T-asymptotic comparison.
Take the infimum over causal learners knowing G, then the supremum over hidden outcome sequences o_1:T.
Expectation is over learner randomness only; comparison is with the best fixed action in hindsight.
guarantees.quantifier_order: One learning algorithm must apply to every instance in the declared class. It may use public inputs only, not hidden instance parameters.
guarantees.time_uniformity: The T-round horizon is fixed and public. No anytime or simultaneous-all-T high-probability guarantee is implied.
description_paragraphs:
$$
R_T^*(G)=\inf_{\mathcal{A}\,\mathrm{knowing}\,G}\sup_{o_{1:T}\in[M]^T}\mathbb{E}_{\mathcal{A}}[R_T]
$$

Choose one algorithm using public inputs before taking the worst case over all admissible instances. Expectation covers the algorithm's private randomness and the observation randomness specified by the model. Comparator choice and the order of summation, minimization, and expectation follow the displayed formula.

objects.definition: The hidden outcome sequence o₁:T ∈ [M]^T is fixed before interaction.
The matrix L ∈ [0,1]^{K×M} is public. Its entry L(a,o) is the loss for action a and outcome o.
The finite signal map H:[K]×[M]→Sigma is public; only H(a_t,o_t) is returned as feedback.
The public game G=(L,H) is fixed; these tables determine its geometry and observability.

variable_blocks.space: The hidden outcome $o_t\in[M]$ is chosen by the environment and is not a learner-controlled query variable.

norms.definition: The model specifies coordinate ranges of finite vectors. Discrete action labels have no derivative order. A placeholder norm imposes no additional geometric assumption.

protocols.adversary_information: The environment fixes the entire loss sequence before interaction. It may know the algorithm and public parameters but cannot depend on the learner’s private seed. This is an oblivious-adversary specification and does not automatically extend to history-dependent adaptive adversaries.
protocols.loss_bearing_points: Only a_t incurs L(a_t,o_t). Incurring a loss does not imply observing it.
protocols.queries_per_round: One signal is observed per round, for T signal events. No fictitious gradient or function-value charges are introduced.
protocols.past_requery: The learner may not request new information from past rounds or previously used samples. Previously received feedback may be stored and processed. In stochastic models, an action may be repeated in a new round, using a fresh charged sample.

parameters.meaning: Minimum uniform-norm bound needed to represent neighboring-action loss differences
parameters.domain: $v\ge0$, finite on the corresponding observable branch.
parameters.definition: For each neighboring action pair a,b choose $h_{ab}:[K]\times\Sigma_H\to\mathbb R$ so that $L(a,o)-L(b,o)=\sum_{c=1}^K h_{ab}(c,H(c,o))$ holds for every outcome o. The value v is the smallest number satisfying $\|h_{ab}\|_\infty\le v$ simultaneously. The locally observable branch restricts the construction to local actions.

evidence.supports: Supports the stated results and explicit reductions: $\mathcal{R}_T^*(G)\ge0$; $\mathcal{R}_T^*(G)\ge c(G)\sqrt T$; $\mathcal{R}_T^*(G)\ge c(G)T^{2/3}$; $\mathcal{R}_T^*(G)\ge c(G)T$. Each bound retains its own model, feedback, parameter region, and quantifiers.
notes: Nondegenerate finite games fall into four regret-rate classes according to their information structure: zero, $\sqrt T$, $T^{2/3}$, and $T$. The lower-bound constructions cover randomized policies. Asymptotics hold for each fixed game, with constants that may depend on the game.

evidence.supports: Supports the stated results and explicit reductions: $\mathcal{R}_T^*(G)\le0$; $\mathcal{R}_T^*(G)\le K^{3/2}(M+1)\sqrt{8T\log K}$; $\mathcal{R}_T^*(G)\le3(TKv)^{2/3}\left(\frac{\log K}{2}\right)^{1/3}$; $\mathcal{R}_T^*(G)\le T$. Each bound retains its own model, feedback, parameter region, and quantifiers.
notes: This classifies a fixed game. The locally observable upper bound is $K^{3/2}(M+1)\sqrt{8T\log K}$ and globally observable upper bound $3(TKv)^{2/3}(\log K/2)^{1/3}$. Source game-dependent constants remain fixed.
